title: Circular timelike orbit and reduced radial stability

items.title: Lyapunov stability of Schwarzschild circular orbits in the fixed-angular-momentum radial system
items.statement:
Adopt the Schwarzschild vacuum exterior model with $m_*>0$, $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$, together with its ideal-free-fall rule that a massive test body follows a future timelike geodesic. For a fixed angular-momentum magnitude $\ell>0$, set

$$W_\ell(r)=f(r)\left(c^2+\frac{\ell^2}{r^2}\right),\qquad r>s.$$

The equatorial reduced radial system is

$$\dot r=w,\qquad \dot w=-\frac12 W_\ell'(r),$$

where dot denotes proper-time derivative and $\ell$ is held fixed. Use SI: $r,s$ are lengths in metres, proper time $\tau$ is in seconds, $w=dr/d\tau$ and $c$ are speeds in metres per second, $\ell$ has units square metres per second, and $W_\ell$ has units squared speed. Lyapunov stability means the Euclidean definition of [[def-cm-equilibrium-and-lyapunov-stability]] applied to the dimensionless state $(q,v)=(r/s,w/c)$ and time $T=c\tau/s$. Equivalently, the distance between radial states is $d((r,w),(\widetilde r,\widetilde w))=\sqrt{((r-\widetilde r)/s)^2+((w-\widetilde w)/c)^2}$. For every circular timelike radius $r_c>3s/2$, the corresponding equilibrium is

$$z_c=(r_c,0),\qquad \ell^2=\frac{c^2s r_c^2}{2r_c-3s}.$$

Then this equilibrium is Lyapunov stable in these dimensionless Euclidean coordinates when $r_c>3s$, and is not Lyapunov stable when $3s/2<r_c\le3s$. At $r_c=3s$ the equilibrium is a stationary inflection of $W_\ell$, not a strict extremum, and is still not Lyapunov stable. These are conclusions about the reduced radial system at fixed $\ell$ only.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 172–179

items.physical_scope: Conditional conclusion of the adopted Schwarzschild vacuum and free-fall model for the one-dimensional timelike radial subsystem at fixed angular momentum. Lyapunov stability is only for the reduced state (r, dr/dτ); it is not stability of the full spacetime orbit, against angular-momentum perturbations, or against radiation reaction, self-force, finite-size effects, or observations.

items.title: Null geodesic radial first integral in the Schwarzschild exterior
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the Schwarzschild exterior datum with $s>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$ on $r>s$, with the countable-choice hypothesis of its geometric suppliers. Let $\gamma:J\to M$ be a smooth affinely parametrized geodesic of its metric-selected connection on a real interval $J$ with nonempty interior, with nonzero tangent and $g(\gamma',\gamma')=0$, whose image lies in the equatorial plane $\vartheta=\pi/2$. Orient its affine parameter toward the future, so that

$$E:=f(r)\frac{dx^0}{d\lambda}>0,\qquad L:=r^2\frac{d\varphi}{d\lambda}\in\mathbb R.$$

Both quantities are constant along $\gamma$. Reversing the affine parameter changes both signs and does not change $L/E$; no sign restriction on $L$ is imposed in the fixed longitude convention. With nonnegative impact parameter $b:=|L|/E$ and $H(r):=f(r)/r^2$, its radial equation is

$$\left(\frac{dr}{d\lambda}\right)^2=E^2\bigl(1-b^2H(r)\bigr).$$

Moreover, $H'(r)=(3s-2r)/r^4$, so $H$ has its unique exterior maximum at $r_{\rm ph}=3s/2$, with $H(r_{\rm ph})=4/(27s^2)$. Thus the critical impact parameter for a radial turning point is $b_{\rm c}=3\sqrt3\,s/2$.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 176–179

items.title: Schwarzschild null scattering and critical impact, with conditional Kruskal capture
items.statement:
Adopt the Schwarzschild exterior vacuum model with $s>0$ and the ideal-light rule that rays are future null geodesics. For an equatorial incoming ray with constants $E>0$, $L\ge0$, impact parameter $b=L/E$, and

$$H(r)=\frac{1-s/r}{r^2},\qquad b_{\rm c}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}s,\qquad r_{\rm ph}=\frac32s,$$

the radial first integral is $\dot r^2=E^2[1-b^2H(r)]$ as in [[lem-rpm-schwarzschild-null-geodesic-reduction]], where dot denotes affine-parameter derivative. Then:

1. If $b>b_{\rm c}$, there is a unique outer turning point $r_*(b)>r_{\rm ph}$, which is reached in finite affine parameter; the ray from infinity turns and returns to infinity. Its total azimuthal advance is

   $$\Delta\varphi=2\int_{r_*}^{\infty}\frac{b\,dr}{r^2\sqrt{1-b^2H(r)}}.$$

   This integral converges at both endpoints.
2. If $b=b_{\rm c}$, the incoming branch from infinity approaches $r_{\rm ph}$ only as affine parameter tends to $+\infty$; its azimuthal advance diverges logarithmically.
3. If $0\le b<b_{\rm c}$, the inward branch has no exterior turning point and reaches the boundary $r=s$ of the Schwarzschild exterior in finite affine parameter. Only if the ray is continued in the specified Kruskal model, once it lies in the region $U\ge0$, does the causal escape result imply that it cannot return to the right exterior.

These are geodesic-model deductions. The impact threshold is not by itself an observable shadow radius.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 176–179

items.physical_scope: Conditional geodesic predictions for ideal rays in the adopted Schwarzschild exterior model. Capture beyond r=s is asserted only conditionally in the named Kruskal extension. The statement excludes finite wavelength, wave optics, source/apparatus modelling, plasma, rotation, self-gravity, and empirical shadow or lensing claims.

items.title: Static-clock redshift, proper acceleration, and a controlled weak-field expansion in Schwarzschild
items.statement:
Adopt the Schwarzschild exterior vacuum model datum $(M,g,N)$ of [[pthm-gr-schwarzschild-vacuum-model]] with $m_*>0$, $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$. Let $r_E,r_R>s$ be the emitter and receiver radii of static observers in this model. Let $\Delta t\ne0$ be a common Schwarzschild coordinate-time duration over which ideal clocks on these static worldlines accrue proper-time increments $\Delta\tau_E$ and $\Delta\tau_R$. For the frequency ratio, let $\eta:J\to M$ be a specified smooth, affinely parametrized future-directed null geodesic in the exterior and choose $\lambda_E<\lambda_R$ in $J$ so that $\eta(\lambda_E)$ and $\eta(\lambda_R)$ lie on the static worldlines at radii $r_E$ and $r_R$, respectively. Let $\omega_E$ and $\omega_R$ be the ideal geometric-optics frequencies assigned by the corresponding static observers at these endpoint events, using the model's geometric-optics identification with observer energy. With $n=f^{-1/2}\partial_0$ the unit static congruence and $U=cn$ the corresponding four-velocity, the ideal-clock and geometric-optics predictions are

$$\frac{\Delta\tau_R}{\Delta\tau_E}=\frac{\omega_E}{\omega_R}=\sqrt{\frac{f(r_R)}{f(r_E)}},\qquad \frac{\omega_R}{\omega_E}=\sqrt{\frac{f(r_E)}{f(r_R)}}.$$

The proper four-acceleration magnitude required to remain static at radius $r>s$ is

$$a(r)=\sqrt{g(\nabla_UU,\nabla_UU)}=\frac{c^2s}{2r^2\sqrt{f(r)}}=\frac{G_Nm_*}{r^2\sqrt{1-s/r}}.$$

For any $0\le\rho<1$ and radii satisfying $0<s/r_E,s/r_R\le\rho$, define $x_i=s/r_i$ and write $\log:=L$ for the natural integral logarithm of [[def-integral-logarithm]]. The exact logarithmic ratio has the uniform expansion

$$\log\frac{\omega_R}{\omega_E}=\frac{s}{2}\left(\frac1{r_R}-\frac1{r_E}\right)+R,\qquad |R|\le\frac{x_E^2+x_R^2}{4(1-\rho)}.$$

These are conditional deductions of the idealized model; no measured redshift or acceleration is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 180–181

items.physical_scope: Conditional model prediction for ideal static clocks, observer energy/frequency ratios in geometric optics, and the proper acceleration required to remain static in the Schwarzschild exterior. The weak-field statement is a uniform mathematical remainder bound. No clock, spectral, acceleration, or gravitational-field measurement is asserted.

items.title: Repulsive relativistic Coulomb Hamiltonian phase system
items.statement:
Let $m,c,\kappa>0$, let $x,p\in\mathbb R^3$, and set

$$D:=(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})\times\mathbb R^3,\qquad r:=|x|,\qquad \mathcal E(p):=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|p|^2}.$$

The **repulsive relativistic Coulomb Hamiltonian** is

$$H(x,p):=\mathcal E(p)+\frac{\kappa}{r},$$

and its **phase system** is the autonomous ODE on the open set $D$

$$\dot x=\nabla_pH=\frac{c^2p}{\mathcal E(p)},\qquad \dot p=-\nabla_xH=\frac{\kappa x}{r^3}.$$

Here the system parameter $t$ is time in seconds and dot denotes $d/dt$; $m$ is a positive mass parameter (kilograms in the SI interpretation), $c$ a positive speed parameter (metres per second), and $\kappa$ a positive energy-times-length parameter (joule-metres). Define the radial momentum $p_r:=x\cdot p/r$ and angular-momentum vector $J:=x\times p$. A trajectory is a $C^1$ map $z=(x,p):I\to D$ on a real interval $I$ with nonempty interior, satisfying this ODE in the interval-solution sense of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. A trajectory $\widetilde z:\widetilde I\to D$ **extends** $z$ if $I\subseteq\widetilde I$ and $\widetilde z|_I=z$; it is a **proper extension** if $I\subsetneq\widetilde I$. A trajectory is **maximal** if it has no proper extension as a solution of this same system in $D$. This definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of maximal trajectories.

This is only a mathematical phase system. Its physical interpretation as a charged particle in an externally prescribed Coulomb field requires separate model assumptions.

references.title: L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, The Classical Theory of Fields, 3rd revised English edition, §39 and Problem 1
Timothy H. Boyer, “Unfamiliar trajectories for a relativistic particle in a Kepler or Coulomb potential,” Am. J. Phys. 72 (2004), arXiv:physics/0405090v1, complete paper

items.physical_scope: Pure mathematical definition of a smooth relativistic phase-space ODE with repulsive inverse-radius potential. It does not identify parameters with measured quantities or assert an electromagnetic model.

items.title: The sine-to-angle limit at the origin
items.statement:
The limit over nonzero real $x$ is

$$\lim_{x\to0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1.$$
items.physical_scope: Pure real-analysis limit used to identify the impact parameter from the asymptotic angular gap; it is not a physical assumption.

references.title: OpenStax, Calculus Volume 1, §2.3 The Limit Laws, unit-circle squeeze proof of the fundamental sine limit

items.title: Reciprocal positive arguments of the principal inverse tangent
items.statement:
For every $y>0$,

$$\arctan y+\arctan(1/y)=\frac{\pi}{2},$$

where $\arctan$ takes values in $(-\pi/2,\pi/2)$.
items.physical_scope: Pure trigonometric identity for the principal inverse tangent; it is used only to rewrite a formal model limit.

references.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §4.23 Inverse Trigonometric Functions, principal values and reflection formulas
OpenStax, Precalculus 2e, §6.3 Inverse Trigonometric Functions

items.title: Exact repulsive relativistic Coulomb scattering branch
items.statement:
Consider the phase system of [[def-rpm-relativistic-coulomb-phase-system]] with $m,c,\kappa>0$. Let a trajectory have conserved energy $W>mc^2$ and angular-momentum magnitude $J:=|x\times p|>\kappa/c$. Define

$$A:=\frac{W^2-m^2c^4}{c^2}>0,\qquad d:=\frac{W\kappa}{c^2}>0,\qquad C:=J^2-\frac{\kappa^2}{c^2}>0.$$

Then its squared radial momentum is

$$p_r^2=Q(u):=A-2du-Cu^2,\qquad u:=1/r.$$

There is a unique positive simple root

$$u_*:=\frac{\sqrt{d^2+CA}-d}{C},\qquad 0<u_*<\frac{W-mc^2}{\kappa}.$$

Every trajectory through the turning data $r_*=1/u_*$, $p_r=0$, and $|x\times p|=J$ has a unique maximal extension defined for all system times $t\in\mathbb R$, in the extension sense of [[def-rpm-relativistic-coulomb-phase-system]]. This extension has one noncollision periapsis and is asymptotically incoming and outgoing. Its impact parameter, defined as the limiting perpendicular distance of either asymptote from the force center, is

$$b=\frac{J}{\sqrt A}>0.$$

If $\Delta$ is the positive azimuthal change from either asymptote to periapsis, then

$$\Delta=\frac{J}{\sqrt C}\arctan\left(\frac{\sqrt{CA}}{d}\right),\qquad \theta:=\pi-2\Delta\in(0,\pi),$$

where $\theta$ is the angle between the incoming and outgoing asymptotic velocity vectors. This formula is for the repulsive branch $J>\kappa/c$; it does not cover $J\le\kappa/c$.

references.title: L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, The Classical Theory of Fields, 3rd revised English edition, §39 and Problem 1
Timothy H. Boyer, “Unfamiliar trajectories for a relativistic particle in a Kepler or Coulomb potential,” Am. J. Phys. 72 (2004), arXiv:physics/0405090v1, complete paper

items.physical_scope: Exact mathematical scattering result for the defined one-body Hamiltonian phase system on a noncolliding repulsive branch. It asserts no electromagnetic derivation, recoil, radiation, measurement, or empirical applicability.

items.title: Exact repulsive relativistic Coulomb scattering in the fixed-source test-body model
items.statement:
Use the charged test-body quantities of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]] on the flat Minkowski specialization, with constant mass $m>0$ in kilograms and constant charge $q$ in coulombs. In a named inertial SI chart write $x^0=ct$, $t\in I:=\mathbb R$, and $\mathbf x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\Omega:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, with $r:=|\mathbf x|>0$; the fixed point source of charge $Q$ in coulombs is at $\mathbf x=0$, which is excluded from the spacetime domain $O:=I\times\Omega$. The prescribed static scalar potential $\phi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, electric field $\mathbf E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and magnetic field $\mathbf B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ are $C^\infty$ on that domain and are

$$\phi(\mathbf x,t)=\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r},\qquad \mathbf E(\mathbf x,t)=\frac{Q\mathbf x}{4\pi\varepsilon_0r^3},\qquad \mathbf B(\mathbf x,t)=0.$$

Here $\varepsilon_0>0$ is the framework SI parameter of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\phi$ has units volts, $\mathbf E$ volts per metre, and $\mathbf B$ teslas. The external four-potential on $O$ has components $A_0=-\phi/c$, $A_i=0$ in the $x^0=ct$ convention, and the electromagnetic two-form convention is that of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]. Thus $E_i=-\partial_{x^i}\phi$ and $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ on $O$; $A$ is $C^\infty$ there and no field value or smoothness across $\mathbf x=0$ is asserted. Put $\kappa:=qQ/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)>0$, which has units joule metres.

The body's worldline is the $C^2$ future-timelike curve $z:I_z\to O$ of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], with $I_z$ an open proper-time interval and tangent $U=dz/d\tau$ satisfying $g(U,U)=-c^2$; its four-momentum is $P=mU$.

Under the adopted fixed-endpoint charged-particle action and its proved Lorentz-force consequence, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure as required by those suppliers. In the flat specialization also adopt the massive-particle momentum model of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]. For $\mathbf v:=d\mathbf x/dt$ one has $|\mathbf v|<c$ and $\gamma:=(1-|\mathbf v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. Then the canonical spatial momentum equals the kinetic momentum $\mathbf p=m\gamma\mathbf v$ (in kilograms metres per second), and the coordinate-time Hamiltonian is

$$H(\mathbf x,\mathbf p)=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}+\frac{\kappa}{r}.$$

Thus the trajectories are those of [[def-rpm-relativistic-coulomb-phase-system]], with $\mathbf x\in\Omega$, $\mathbf p\in\mathbb R^3$, and coordinate time $t\in I$. For asymptotic scattering data, use the unique maximal coordinate-time extension of the given local phase trajectory on the noncolliding scattering branch of that phase system. Incoming and outgoing asymptotic vectors below belong to this extension; a finite interval restriction need not itself contain either asymptotic tail. Let $W:=H(\mathbf x,\mathbf p)>mc^2$ be its conserved energy in joules and let $J:=|\mathbf x\times\mathbf p|>\kappa/c$ be the conserved angular-momentum magnitude in kilograms metres squared per second. The proposition [[prop-rpm-relativistic-coulomb-scattering-branch]] gives the incoming and outgoing asymptotic velocity vectors and defines their principal Euclidean angle $\theta\in(0,\pi)$ as $\pi-2\Delta$; the limiting momentum vectors have the same directions because $\mathbf p=m\gamma\mathbf v$ with $\gamma>0$. Define

$$\mathcal A=\frac{W^2-m^2c^4}{c^2},\qquad d=\frac{W\kappa}{c^2},\qquad C=J^2-\frac{\kappa^2}{c^2},$$

Here $\mathcal A$ is the positive scalar denoted $A$ in [[prop-rpm-relativistic-coulomb-scattering-branch]]. Its exact angle between incoming and outgoing momenta is

$$\theta=\pi-\frac{2J}{\sqrt C}\arctan\left(\frac{\sqrt{C\mathcal A}}{d}\right)\in(0,\pi).$$

Here $\mathcal A$ has units of squared momentum, $d$ has units of $\mathcal A$ times length, and $C$ has units of squared angular momentum, so $\sqrt{C\mathcal A}/d$ and $\theta$ are dimensionless. This is a model deduction, not a measured scattering law. The inequality $J>\kappa/c$ is part of the result's domain; no conclusion is made for $J\le\kappa/c$.

references.title: L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, The Classical Theory of Fields, 3rd revised English edition, §§16–17, 19, 39 and Problem 1
Timothy H. Boyer, “Unfamiliar trajectories for a relativistic particle in a Kepler or Coulomb potential,” Am. J. Phys. 72 (2004), arXiv:physics/0405090v1, complete paper

items.physical_scope: Conditional model deduction for a single massive charged test body in flat spacetime moving in a prescribed, fixed, repulsive point-source Coulomb field, under the explicitly stated ACω and flat massive-particle assumptions. The exact angle applies only for W>mc² and J>κ/c. Source recoil, radiation, self-field, collisions, measurement, and empirical applicability are excluded.

title: Circular timelike orbit and reduced radial stability — Examples

items.title: Fixed-angular-momentum stability at 2s, 3s and 4s
items.statement:
Use $s>0$ and the reduced potential $W_\ell(r)=(1-s/r)(c^2+\ell^2/r^2)$ of [[pthm-rpm-schwarzschild-circular-stability]]. At a circular orbit, $\ell^2=c^2sr_0^2/(2r_0-3s)$.

1. **Stable radial equilibrium at $r_0=4s$.** The circular value is $\ell^2=16c^2s^2/5$, and

   $$W_\ell''(4s)=\frac{2c^2s(4s-3s)}{(4s)^3(8s-3s)}=\frac{c^2}{160s^2}>0.$$

   The fixed-$\ell$ radial equilibrium is Lyapunov stable.
2. **Unstable radial equilibrium at $r_0=2s$.** Here $\ell^2=4c^2s^2$ and

   $$W_\ell''(2s)=\frac{2c^2s(2s-3s)}{(2s)^3(4s-3s)}=-\frac{c^2}{4s^2}<0.$$

   The fixed-$\ell$ equilibrium is unstable.
3. **Degenerate endpoint at $r_0=3s$.** Here $\ell^2=3c^2s^2$ and $W_\ell'(r)=c^2s(r-3s)^2/r^4$. It has a stationary inflection rather than a strict extremum, and the radial equilibrium is not Lyapunov stable by the one-sided perturbation argument in the theorem.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 174–177

items.physical_scope: Worked parameter values for the conditional Schwarzschild fixed-angular-momentum radial model; not full orbital stability or an observation.

items.title: An exact turning ray and the critical Schwarzschild impact parameter
items.statement:
Use the SI Schwarzschild convention of the scattering model: $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2>0$ and the areal radius $r>s$ are lengths in metres, with $m_*$ in kilograms, $G_N$ in cubic metres per kilogram per squared second, and $c$ in metres per second. The impact parameters $b,b_c$ are also lengths in metres; $H(r)=(1-s/r)/r^2$ has units inverse square metres, so $b^2H(r)$ is dimensionless. No numerical mass or measured length is stipulated. Take the incoming equatorial future-null rays with $E>0$ and $L\ge0$ of the scattering supplier, so $b=L/E=|L|/E$. The critical impact parameter is $b_c=3\sqrt3s/2$. Choose $b=2\sqrt2s>b_c$. The radial factor is $1-b^2(1-s/r)/r^2$.

1. At $r=2s$, this factor is $1-(8s^2)(1/2)/(4s^2)=0$. Because $2s>3s/2$ and $H(r)=(1-s/r)/r^2$ is strictly decreasing for $r>3s/2$, $r_*=2s$ is the unique outer turning point. The ideal incoming ray turns there and returns outward.
2. At the critical value, direct factorization gives

   $$1-b_c^2H(r)=\frac{(2r-3s)^2(r+3s)}{4r^3}.$$

   Thus the critical inward ray from infinity approaches $r=3s/2$ asymptotically, and the azimuthal integral diverges logarithmically; it does not complete a finite number of windings before reaching the circular orbit in affine parameter.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 177–179

items.physical_scope: Exact Schwarzschild exterior geodesic example for the ideal-light model. It is not a finite-resolution image or measured lensing result.

items.title: Static Schwarzschild clocks at 2s and 4s, and the near-horizon acceleration limit
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the adopted Schwarzschild exterior datum with $s>0$ and $f(r)=1-s/r$. Compare ideal static clocks at radii $r_E=2s$ and $r_R=4s$ over a common Schwarzschild coordinate-time interval of duration $\Delta t>0$. For the frequency ratio, choose a specified smooth, affinely parametrized future-directed null geodesic $\eta:J\to M$ in the exterior with endpoint parameters $\lambda_E<\lambda_R$ on those static worldlines, and use the ideal geometric-optics frequencies assigned by the endpoint static observers. Here $f(2s)=1/2$ and $f(4s)=3/4$.

1. The exact model ratios are

   $$\frac{\omega_R}{\omega_E}=\sqrt{\frac{f(2s)}{f(4s)}}=\sqrt{\frac23},\qquad \frac{\Delta\tau_R}{\Delta\tau_E}=\sqrt{\frac{f(4s)}{f(2s)}}=\sqrt{\frac32}.$$

   The static proper acceleration at $2s$ is $a(2s)=c^2/(4\sqrt2s)$.
2. Write $r=s(1+\epsilon)$ for $\epsilon>0$. The exact static proper acceleration is

   $$a(r)=\frac{c^2}{2s\sqrt\epsilon(1+\epsilon)^{3/2}},$$

   which tends to $+\infty$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$. In contrast, the curvature scalar has limit $K\to12/s^4$ by [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-curvature-and-kretschmann-scalar]], and the advanced extension chart is smooth through $r=s$ by [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]]. The acceleration divergence is therefore a property of maintaining a static worldline near the boundary, not evidence of a curvature blow-up there.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, author-hosted Chapter 1 HTML of the complete lecture notes, §§1.2.5 and 1.3.1–1.3.5 (printed pp. 24–46)
Sean Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, complete lecture notes, §7, pp. 180–181

items.physical_scope: Worked model calculation for ideal static observers and an ideal light ray. The near-horizon acceleration is a model requirement for static motion, not an observation; curvature and extension statements are geometric properties of the specified Schwarzschild model.

items.title: Formal nonrelativistic limit of the repulsive Coulomb scattering angle
items.statement:
Fix $m,\kappa,K,b>0$ and let $c\to\infty$ with $W_c=mc^2+K$ and $J_c=b\sqrt{A_c}$, where $A_c=(W_c^2-m^2c^4)/c^2$. For sufficiently large $c$, $J_c>\kappa/c$ because $J_c^2-\kappa^2/c^2\to2mKb^2>0$.

1. The relativistic scattering angle tends to the nonrelativistic repulsive Coulomb angle:

   $$\theta_c\longrightarrow2\arctan\left(\frac{\kappa}{2Kb}\right).$$

   This agrees with [[thm-cm-coulomb-scattering]] at kinetic energy $K$ and impact parameter $b$.
2. The limit compares ideal mathematical model formulas while holding the indicated parameters fixed; it supplies no experimental evidence for either model.

references.title: L. D. Landau and E. M. Lifshitz, The Classical Theory of Fields, 3rd revised English edition, §39 and Problem 1
Timothy H. Boyer, “Unfamiliar trajectories for a relativistic particle in a Kepler or Coulomb potential,” Am. J. Phys. 72 (2004), arXiv:physics/0405090v1, complete paper

items.physical_scope: Formal c-to-infinity limit of exact model formulas at fixed rest mass, Coulomb coupling, Newtonian kinetic energy, and impact parameter. It is not a measured comparison or empirical validation.
